config.title: Express performance

intro.title: Express performance
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Express server that uses built-in performance techniques to handle requests faster. You will learn the core concept of middleware chaining to optimize response times by minimizing processing steps. The main technologies involved are the Express framework, its routing system, and the native Node.js HTTP module. By the end, you'll understand how to structure an application for better speed and efficiency, which is essential for any web service.
intro.usecase: Express performance optimization is crucial for high-traffic applications like e-commerce platforms during flash sales, where thousands of users simultaneously browse products and add items to carts. In social media dashboards, optimized Express servers ensure real-time updates load instantly as users scroll through feeds and notifications. API-driven admin panels rely on performance tuning to handle complex data filtering and reporting queries without lag. Developers implement these techniques to prevent slowdowns during peak usage, ensuring responsive user experiences across web applications.

objectives: Configure Express middleware to compress HTTP responses
Implement caching headers for static assets to reduce server load
Construct a route handler that efficiently streams large files
Apply environment-based configuration to toggle performance features
Integrate a logging middleware to monitor request-response timing
Manipulate response objects to set appropriate performance headers
Initialize a production-ready Express server with performance optimizations

steps.title: Import Express and required middleware modules
steps.instruction: Import Express, compression, and helmet modules for the application.
steps.hint: Use the require() function to import each module. You'll need to import express, compression, and helmet.
steps.seedCode: // Import Express, compression, and helmet modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The application will have access to Express and performance-related middleware modules.
successCriteria: Express, compression, and helmet are imported using require().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You imported some modules, but make sure to import Express, compression, and helmet.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statements. You need to import Express, compression, and helmet using require().

steps.title: Initialize Express application instance
steps.instruction: Create an Express application instance by calling the imported Express function and assign it to a constant named 'app'.
steps.hint: Use the imported Express module to create your application instance with a function call.
steps.analogousExample:
// Creating an application instance
const app = express();
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have an Express application instance ready to configure with middleware and routes.
successCriteria: An Express application instance is created and assigned to a constant named 'app'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're creating the application instance with the imported Express module and assigning it to 'app'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The application instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to call the imported Express function to create the instance.

steps.title: Set up compression middleware for response size reduction
steps.instruction: Use the compression middleware you imported to compress HTTP responses by calling app.use() with compression() as the argument.
steps.hint: Remember that app.use() adds middleware to your Express application. Pass the compression function (without arguments) as the middleware.
steps.expectedOutcome: The compression middleware will be applied to all incoming requests, automatically compressing response bodies when supported by the client.
successCriteria: The app.use() method is called with compression() as its argument to enable response compression.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.use() with the compression middleware function.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to use app.use(compression()) to enable response compression.

steps.title: Configure helmet middleware for security headers
steps.instruction: Use the helmet middleware on your Express app to automatically set security headers.
steps.hint: Call app.use() with helmet() as the argument, similar to how you used compression middleware.
steps.expectedOutcome: The helmet middleware will be applied to all incoming requests, adding security headers that improve both security and performance.
successCriteria: helmet middleware is correctly applied using app.use(helmet())
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're calling app.use() with helmet() as the argument. The helmet middleware needs to be invoked as a function.
steps.feedbackWrong: The helmet middleware isn't properly configured. You need to use app.use(helmet()) to apply the middleware to your Express application.

steps.title: Create a basic route handler for the root path
steps.instruction: Define a GET route handler for the root path ('/') that sends a simple text response.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with '/' as the path and a callback that sends a response with res.send().
steps.expectedOutcome: A GET route for the root path is defined and ready to respond.
successCriteria: The route handler uses app.get() with '/' as the path and sends a response with res.send().
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using app.get() with '/' and sending a response with res.send().
steps.feedbackWrong: The route handler isn't defined correctly. Check the path and response method.

steps.title: Add static file serving middleware
steps.instruction: Configure Express to serve static files from a 'public' directory using the built-in express.static middleware.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with express.static() and pass the directory name as a string.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: serving static files from a folder named 'assets'
app.use(express.static('assets'));
steps.expectedOutcome: The app will be able to serve static files (like HTML, CSS, images) from a 'public' directory.
successCriteria: express.static middleware is configured to serve files from the 'public' directory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using express.static() and specifying the correct directory name.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to use the built-in express.static middleware to serve files from a directory.

steps.title: Implement response caching headers
steps.instruction: Add middleware to set cache-control headers for static assets served by Express.
steps.hint: Use app.use() with a custom middleware function that sets the Cache-Control header on responses.
steps.expectedOutcome: The application will include middleware that sets Cache-Control headers for browser caching of static assets.
successCriteria: Middleware is added that sets the Cache-Control header with a max-age value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added middleware, but make sure it sets the Cache-Control header with appropriate values like 'public, max-age=3600'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The caching middleware is missing or incorrect. Try adding app.use() with a function that sets res.setHeader('Cache-Control', ...).

steps.title: Create a performance monitoring route
steps.instruction: Define a GET route handler for '/performance' that returns a JSON response with performance data.
steps.hint: Use app.get() with '/performance' as the path and a callback function that sends a JSON response containing performance-related data.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new route at '/performance' that returns JSON data when accessed via GET request.
successCriteria: A GET route for '/performance' is defined with app.get() and returns a JSON response containing performance-related data.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a route, but make sure it's a GET route for '/performance' and returns JSON with performance data.
steps.feedbackWrong: The route isn't defined correctly. Check that you're using app.get() with '/performance' and returning JSON.

steps.title: Start the Express server
steps.instruction: Make your Express application listen on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use the app.listen() method with the port number and an optional callback function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The Express server will be configured to start listening for incoming requests on port 3000.
successCriteria: The app.listen() method is called with port 3000 and optionally includes a callback function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling app.listen() with port 3000. You can optionally add a callback function to log a message when the server starts.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly configured to start. You need to call app.listen() with port 3000 to make the application listen for requests.

steps.title: Test the application with different endpoints
steps.instruction: Test your Express application by running it and accessing the root route, static files, and performance route to verify the performance optimizations are working.
steps.hint: Start your server with node index.js, then open your browser or use curl to visit http://localhost:3000/, http://localhost:3000/performance, and any static file you've placed in your public folder.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should be able to access all three endpoints and observe performance improvements like compressed responses, security headers, and caching headers in the network tab.
successCriteria: The application runs successfully and all three endpoints (root, static files, performance) respond with the expected performance optimizations visible.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started testing, but make sure to check all three endpoints (root, static files, performance) and verify the optimizations in the response headers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The testing didn't go as expected. Make sure your server is running, then visit http://localhost:3000/, http://localhost:3000/performance, and try accessing a static file to see if the optimizations are working.
